The negative side is mostly inferential from opaque spending and severe hardship, not from a smoking-gun patronage document.","evidence":[{"title":"With Good Governance and Commitment, We must Overcomee Old Subsidy Benficiaries- President Tinubu","publisher":"State House","date":"March 15, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/with-good-governance-and-commitment-we-must-overcomee-old-subsidy-benificiaries-president-tinubu/","summary":"Tinubu framed subsidy reform as a way to fund student loans, consumer credit, and social welfare, said the treasury must not be abused, and stressed using NIN-linked data to target relief. This is strong positive evidence of a broad-based, programmatic intent rather than rent distribution.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"IMF Executive Board Concludes Post Financing Assessment with Nigeria","publisher":"IMF","date":"February 9, 2024","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa","summary":"The IMF said Tinubu moved ahead with fuel-subsidy removal and FX unification, created a fiscal/tax reform committee, and paired austerity with cereals, subsidized fertilizer, a wage award, and diesel VAT suspension to soften inflation. This supports a reading of reform for fiscal sustainability rather than short-term popularity.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification","publisher":"World Bank","date":"June 13, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification","summary":"The Bank said the reforms were meant to raise non-oil revenues, safeguard oil revenues, and create fiscal space for quality public services, while also rolling out a targeted cash transfer program for 15 million households. That is strong evidence for broad-based, sustainable prosperity as the stated policy goal.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"Turning The Corner: Nigeria’s Ongoing Path of Economic Reforms","publisher":"World Bank","date":"June 13, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms","summary":"The Bank said reforms reduced distortions and improved transparency, especially by eliminating the official/parallel FX gap and phasing out the regressive, opaque fuel subsidy. It also warned that households were absorbing serious cost-of-living pain, so the reforms were pro-sustainability but costly in the short run.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Directs Reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement","publisher":"State House","date":"June 15, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/","summary":"Tinubu ordered a reorganization of the Bureau of Public Procurement to improve efficiency and transparency. This is direct positive evidence against a simple rent-extraction reading.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu: Live Up To Your Expectation As Public Trust For Accountability","publisher":"State House","date":"July 6, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-live-up-to-your-expectation-as-public-trust-for-accountability/","summary":"Tinubu described public institutions as public trust, not personal enterprise, and emphasized merit and accountability in public service. This supports a governance style aimed at institution-building rather than patronage.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu: I have no Cabal or Sponsors to Compensate","publisher":"State House","date":"July 26, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-i-have-no-cabal-or-sponsors-to-compensate/","summary":"Tinubu explicitly denied having a cabal or sponsors to repay and presented the reform program as unconstrained by factional patronage. That is useful anti-loyalty-buying evidence, though it is rhetoric rather than proof of behavior.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"Nigeria’s Tinubu seeks $30 billion budget reset to end overlapping fiscal years","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"December 17, 2025","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigerias-tinubu-seeks-30-billion-budget-reset-to-end-overlapping-fiscal-years-4413424","summary":"Reuters said Tinubu pushed a budget reset to end overlapping fiscal years and tighten controls on public finances. This is later than the target year, but it points in the same direction as the 2024 reform logic: tighter fiscal discipline rather than short-term extraction.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"Nigeria’s Tinubu names seven ministers, sacks five in cabinet reshuffle","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"October 23, 2024","url":"https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/","summary":"Reuters described a normal cabinet reshuffle rather than a purge tied to factional loyalty testing. That is weak but real counterevidence against a loyalty-buying / patronage-maintenance interpretation.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"Nigeria’s cost-of-living protest wave","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"August 1, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376","summary":"Reuters reported that subsidy removal, naira devaluation, and higher electricity tariffs pushed inflation above 34% and eroded incomes, fueling protests over the cost of living and governance. This is strong negative evidence that the reform path imposed harsh short-term pain and was not yet broadly prosperity-producing in practice.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"Insecurity, rising costs push 31 million Nigerians into acute food shortage, study says","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"August 27, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474","summary":"Reuters reported that 31.8 million Nigerians were acutely short of food, with subsidy removal and insecurity cited as major drivers. This is the clearest negative evidence that 2024 policy outcomes were still far from broad-based prosperity.","question_ids":["5B.1"]},{"title":"FG spent N63.6bn on military equipment in seven months-report","publisher":"Punch","date":"August 17, 2024","url":"https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/","summary":"The report said the federal government spent at least N63.6bn on military equipment and special ammunition in the first seven months of 2024, with substantial arms imports and weak disclosure. This is the strongest negative item for the “rent extraction / opacity” side, because it raises transparency and diversion concerns even if it does not prove abuse.","question_ids":["5B.1"]}]}
